title: Localization formula for the specified open reduction mate
statement: Fix l,E, system and realization [def-sf-integral-system-canonical-bridge]. For any open immersion j and any flat-term K-flat representative P [def-a1-flat-term-kflat-complex], there are comparison isomorphisms from the source and target of the specified derived openReduction at Q(P) to the localizations of the source and target of the ordinary open mate [lem-sf-ordinary-open-reduction-mate]. Under these isomorphisms that derived mate is exactly Q of the degreewise ordinary mate, as an equality of whole-system arrows. The source comparison is explicitly the given reduction-model comparison followed by the exact-open derived factorization.

source.place: Maps-used sentence, open-factor normalization: identification with the fixed whole-system mate.

proof.text: Apply openExtension_goodComplex to P to obtain good representatives JP and RJP. Define s as shriek of the reduction-model isomorphism followed by the exact system-open factorization. Define t as reduction of the exact completed-open factorization followed by the reduction-model isomorphism on JP. The defining equation for s is reflexive.

Prove the equality after applying the system open adjunction Hom equivalence and postcomposing with the invertible system-pull factorization. Localization of the exact adjunction identifies its Hom equivalence with Q of the complex Hom equivalence, using the localized ordinary unit. The complex transpose of the ordinary open mate is ordinary reduction of the completed-open complex unit followed by ordinary reductionPull on JP, degreewise by unit_mateEquiv_symm. For the derived mate the same unit identity identifies its transpose with reduction of the derived completed-open unit followed by realization.reductionPull. Use naturality of reductionPull at the completed-open factorization, then realization.model on JP and RJP. The localized unit formula cancels the completed-pull factorization; naturality of pullbackTensorReductionModel on the good-complex unit P to RJP leaves precisely the complex transpose above. Injectivity of the Hom equivalence proves the equality of whole-system arrows.

lean.statement:
theorem openReduction_mate_localization (system : Operations l E)
    (realization : RealizationModel l E system) {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (j : X ⟶ Y) [IsOpenImmersion j]
    (P : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E X).FullSubcategory) :
    ∃ (s : ((calculus l E X).reduction ⋙ Operations.shriek l E system j).obj
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (((system.extension j).ordinary.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
          (((pullbackTensorOrdinaryReduction l E X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
            P.obj)))
      (t : (ringedOpen l E j ⋙ (calculus l E Y).reduction).obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj) ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((pullbackTensorOrdinaryReduction l E Y).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
            ((Functor.mapHomologicalComplex
              (PurCompactSupport.openExtension (PurCompactSupport.completed l E) j)
              (.up ℤ)).obj P.obj))),
      s.hom =
        (Operations.shriek l E system j).map
          ((pullbackTensorReductionModel l E X).hom.app P) ≫
        (system.extension j).ordinary.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app
          (((pullbackTensorOrdinaryReduction l E X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P.obj) ∧
      (realization.openReduction l E j).app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj) ≫ t.hom =
        s.hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map
          (realization.ordinary.openReductionComplex l E j (system.extension j) P.obj)
